  "id": "you-got-her-pregnant",
  "title": "You Got Her Pregnant",
  "description": "Reusable adult pregnancy-and-relationship-consequence engine where {{user}} is the biological father, or is ultimately established as the biological father, of {{char}}'s pregnancy. Includes grouped Direction Presets for the fleshed-out You Got Her Pregnant sub-series.",
  "source_version": "1.2",
  "bible": {},
  "summary": "An adult {{char}} becomes pregnant and {{user}} is the biological father, or is ultimately confirmed to be the biological father. Unlike She Got Pregnant, {{char}} and {{user}} do not need to begin as an established couple: they may be friends, friends with benefits, strangers, rivals, coworkers, affair partners, people already attached to others, participants in a consensual non-monogamous arrangement, donor participants, or people connected through a speculative mechanism. The pregnancy creates or transforms a lasting biological, social and emotional connection.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}} and {{user}} are adults. {{user}} is the biological father of {{char}}'s pregnancy, or a selected direction may begin with genuine uncertainty that later establishes {{user}} as the father. Their prior relationship can range from close friendship or casual sex to an affair, one-time encounter, consensual partner-sharing arrangement, deliberate donor plan, professional or university connection, rivalry, distance relationship, or compatible speculative setup. The pregnancy must materially change the relationship or social situation rather than functioning as a disposable twist.",
  "setup": "Begin near the discovery, confession, paternity confirmation, reunion, first unavoidable consequence, or another strong roleplay opening. Establish enough of {{char}} and {{user}}'s prior connection for the pregnancy to matter, but do not pre-decide {{user}}'s reaction, romantic commitment, parenting choice or relationship outcome.",
  "core_variables": [
    "{{char}}'s relationship to {{user}} before conception: friend, FWB, stranger, rival, coworker, classmate, affair partner, outside partner, donor recipient, public figure, or another compatible role.",
    "Whether {{char}}, {{user}}, both, or neither already has another adult partner.",
    "Whether conception comes from a casual encounter, recurring relationship, affair, consensual non-monogamy, cuckolding/cuckqueen setup, deliberate donor plan, partner swap, travel event, fake relationship, or speculative mechanism.",
    "Whether paternity is immediately certain, only likely, genuinely uncertain, or established later by testing or evidence.",
    "What each adult knew about other relationships, non-exclusivity, contraception, fertility and pregnancy risk beforehand.",
    "Whether the conception itself was accidental, an accepted risk, deliberately attempted, or an unforeseen result of a speculative mechanism.",
    "When {{char}} discovers the pregnancy and when {{user}} learns he may be or is the father.",
    "Whether the reveal occurs directly, remotely, after separation, through testing, through a visible pregnancy, or during a public/professional complication.",
    "What {{char}} wants from {{user}} after the pregnancy: romance, co-parenting, limited involvement, secrecy, distance, support, or an unresolved conversation.",
    "How existing partners, friends, family, workplaces, public audiences or other social relationships complicate the new biological connection."
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Create genuinely different casts, settings, histories, motives and reveal structures rather than cosmetic variations.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual participants must be adults.",
    "{{user}} must be the biological father, the likely/plausible father in a genuinely uncertain-paternity opening, or ultimately established as the biological father when the selected direction specifically uses later confirmation.",
    "Do not turn the source into She Got Pregnant by establishing another man as the biological father while {{user}} is merely the betrayed or social partner.",
    "Do not require {{char}} and {{user}} to begin in an established romantic relationship; one defining strength of this source is that pregnancy can create the permanent connection.",
    "Leave {{user}} free to decide his reaction, romantic commitment, parenting involvement, disclosure choices and next actions.",
    "Do not write {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, intentions, consent or future decisions as settled facts unless a selected preset explicitly supplies a prior factual action.",
    "Do not assume cheating when the selected direction defines an open relationship, cuckolding/cuckqueen dynamic, partner swap, donor arrangement or another mutually agreed route.",
    "Do not assume consent between existing partners when the selected direction explicitly involves secrecy or an affair.",
    "Treat uncertain paternity as genuinely uncertain until the selected direction establishes a result.",
    "Pregnancy and biological fatherhood do not automatically require romance, marriage, cohabitation or a specific parenting arrangement.",
    "If a preset supplies a narrower defining condition, preserve that condition while varying the remaining axes."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All sexual participants are adults.",
    "Do not sexualize minors. Existing or future children may appear only in ordinary family, parenting, household or parentage-related context.",
    "Do not force romance, forgiveness, rejection, co-parenting, marriage, abortion, adoption, secrecy, disclosure or any other major decision from {{user}}.",
    "Clearly distinguish consensual non-monogamy, cuckolding/cuckqueen arrangements, partner swapping and donor plans from cheating.",
    "Clearly distinguish pressure, professional leverage and coercion from voluntary consent; do not treat employment, grades, housing, travel, fame, payment or social pressure as automatic consent.",
    "Alcohol or parties may alter the social setting but must not be used to erase capacity to consent.",
    "Do not assume that biological fatherhood automatically gives {{user}} control over {{char}}'s body, pregnancy decisions, relationships or living arrangements.",
    "Do not present one cosmetic rename, occupation swap or location change as a genuinely new idea."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Friends, FWB, strangers, rivals, coworkers, classmates, affair partners, outside partners, donors or speculative connections",
    "Neither attached, {{char}} attached, {{user}} attached, or both attached",
    "Secret betrayal versus consensual non-monogamy versus deliberate conception versus one-time circumstance",
    "Known fatherhood versus initially uncertain paternity versus later test confirmation",
    "One-time encounter versus recurring casual relationship versus developing romance",
    "Local everyday setting versus university, workplace, travel, public-figure, family-social or speculative setting",
    "Immediate reveal versus delayed message versus reunion versus visible pregnancy versus test-result reveal",
    "{{char}} wants romance, co-parenting, limited involvement, continued independence, secrecy or has not decided",
    "Existing partners stay, leave, cooperate, remain unaware or become part of a negotiated multi-adult family structure",
    "Hopeful, awkward, dramatic, scandalous, emotionally complicated, comedic or speculative tone",
    "Pregnancy creates a romance, creates only a parenting link, exposes an affair, restructures an existing arrangement or leaves the future unresolved"

    {
      "id": "source-boundary",
      "label": "Series scope vs main source",
      "content": "The You Got Her Pregnant main source is deliberately broad about the starting relationship, but it still has one defining invariant: {{user}} is the biological father, a genuinely plausible father before confirmation, or ultimately established as the biological father. If another man is established as the father and {{user}} is only the betrayed or social partner, use She Got Pregnant instead. Very unusual premises whose conception logic cannot be expressed cleanly should be hand-authored or moved to a future companion source rather than weakening the main source."
    },
    {
      "id": "paternity-handling",
      "label": "Paternity handling",
      "content": "Known, likely and uncertain paternity are different story states. Do not convert uncertainty into certainty without the selected direction calling for testing or later evidence. When a preset such as Paternity Test Says {{user}} or She Thought Someone Else Was the Father is selected, the eventual result must establish {{user}} as the biological father."
    },
    {
      "id": "preset-use",
      "label": "Preset use",
      "content": "Use the narrowest relevant Direction Preset. For an even narrower leaf variation, edit the populated Additional Direction with one short visible sentence, such as making a childhood-friend pregnancy come from their first and only encounter, setting fake dating at a family wedding, or specifying that a public figure is an idol."
    }
